title: TRAITORS AND THEIR EXQUISITE SUBTLETY: THE JUDAS ISCARIOT EFFECT

sense.text:
“There is an exquisite subtilty, and the same is unjust.” It is speaking of a person: there is a person of exquisite subtlety.

Exquisite is something of flawless craftsmanship, delicate beauty, or rare and consummate excellence: carefully crafted, very detailed, very intricate, extremely pleasing to the senses, of special beauty or charm, of rare and appealing excellence, like a face, a flower, music or poetry. Add one more thing to that list: a doctrine. A doctrine can be taught in a way where you can’t catch on. It is very deceptive. It is not beautiful, it is charming, appealing, alluring, seductive.

Subtle is something delicate, precise, or difficult to perceive: details, distinctions or changes that are not immediately obvious and take careful thought, keen perception or close attention to notice. As an Israelite you can’t outright say, I’m teaching Christianity. So you have to be very cunning, very slick and very wordy. We don’t teach Christianity. But the nation is going to be saved, though. Then you are teaching Christianity.

Nation salvation is that kind of doctrine. The nation’s going to be saved, there’s some good ones. To the coons out there, and to our people who have Stockholm syndrome and a slave mentality, that is a charming and appealing doctrine: Wow, brother, you’re coming around. Many have low self-esteem and low self-worth and seek salvation for their enemies while those enemies hold them captive. Wanting heaven for your enemies while you are in their hell is a slave mentality.

“And the same is unjust”: the one that is exquisitely subtle is wicked as hell, and you can’t figure it out unless you keep God’s commandments. Without them you won’t see through the deception.

“Yet hath he not root in himself, but dureth for a while”: he endures for a while. “For when tribulation or persecution ariseth because of the word, by and by he is offended.” By and by means over time. It is not immediate, but over time they get offended.

There are a number of different groups this speaks to, and they all tie together: Israelites who are slowly converting, somewhat, back into Christianity, because they want the world and what it has to offer, the finer things in life that come behind covetousness; modern Christians who are somewhat converting to the truth; and individualites who hate camps.

When the one with no root is offended by and by, he leaves and tries to pull down with him whatever he learned. Angry and bitter over his exposure to the world, over what he does at home, over his evil doings and secret actions, he will dismiss, denounce and renounce all that he learned and the community he was once part of.

precepts.why:
“And ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars”: we are in that time now. “See that ye be not troubled”: don’t be troubled by what you see on the news or hear. “For all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet. For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom”, with famines, pestilences and earthquakes. “All these are the beginning of sorrows.” Then the persecutions: “Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all nations for my name’s sake.”

That goes back to “by and by he is offended.” “And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.” Because of the offence, the persecution and the affliction, they betray.

This is the transition. America is going from being a power to losing power, getting weaker and weaker, and inside the nation of Israel (not really a community, more like different factions, with little in common but knowing they are Israel) Israelites are slowly transitioning into Christianity or into the world, while trying to keep elements of Israelite doctrine. Christ said you can’t serve two masters. It starts with they just going to be saved. Because that is a white supremacist doctrine, more comes in over time: no more feast days, no more beard, no more fringes. The 12 tribes chart is wrong. The seals of Revelation haven’t opened yet. America is not really Babylon. The white man is not really Esau, he’s Japheth. It can’t be done outright. It has to be gradual, because they want the world. That is the beginning stage of betrayal.

“And many false prophets shall rise, and shall deceive many”: during the betrayal and the hatred, false prophets arise. “And because iniquity shall abound”: because of these false prophets and false teachings, iniquity grows, because the laws of God will be persecuted and outlawed. The commandments taught in the street, outlawed. They are already passing laws, covertly and overtly, to silence this truth. Israelites who don’t like us but watch the classes are paying attention, positioning themselves so that when the persecution comes they think they’ll be safe: You teach only Israelites are going to be saved, that’s racism.

“The love of many shall wax cold.” Out of that love that waxed cold they begin to hate and betray, become traitors, leave and depart. “But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved. And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations; and then shall the end come.” The one who endures unto the end is saved.

“And at that time there was a great persecution against the church which was at Jerusalem; and they were all scattered abroad throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria, except the apostles.” Many don’t want a great persecution. They think they are going to stay here in America and stand on the corner.

A lot of new camps are popping up: orphan camps, with no elders and no guidance. They watched a few YouTube videos and said, we can do that, in the same uniform, but they are not guided. They are a bunch of kids on the street corners making a name for themselves, cursing out the heathens. After a while laws will be passed saying you cannot teach this no more, and many of the same Israelites who were bold and brave in the street will hide in their houses and become podcast prophets, teaching the Bible on YouTube with their faces blurred.

And the ones who stay steadfast and teach regardless, and get killed, locked up or exiled as the church at Jerusalem was scattered, those Israelites will say, You getting locked up because you wicked. That’s the Lord judging you. They will betray and hate one another as they cower in fear, positioning themselves to be the play-it-safe Israelites: They just going to be saved. I don’t hate anybody. I’m not racist.

“It was necessary that the word of God should first have been spoken to you”: to the southern kingdom Jews. “But seeing ye put it from you”, rejecting it, “and judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting life, lo, we turn to the Gentiles”: to go teach the northern kingdom, our people scattered abroad. “I have set thee to be a light of the Gentiles, that thou shouldest be for salvation unto the ends of the earth”: Israel scattered. “And when the Gentiles heard this, they were glad, and glorified the word of the Lord.” They received it with no problems.

It is the same today. America is the land of privilege, and our people here, in the truth and in the world, have a level of entitlement: I heard that already. Bible, yeah yeah, Israelite, yada yada. Even in the ghetto and the slums there is running water, hot water and a toilet. In Africa and the islands, where our people are poor, they listen, because poverty opens your ears real quick. In Zambia, kids came barefoot out of a brick house with no windows, carrying water and selling their own crops to eat. At least five or six thousand flyers were given out there and not one was on the ground; a little girl picked one up and said, let me get two. A whole day can be spent out there teaching from Revelation that Christ is a black man, over and over, and they smile with pride and joy. Here: he’s Middle Eastern, he’s olive-skinned, he’s a rainbow, who cares what color he is.

At a festival here the flyers were folded, ripped in half and blowing in the wind: Look at these niggers. They are too comfortable here, too immersed. That is why this place has to burn. So the reception is heavier outside the States than here, just as the Jews in Jerusalem rejected it and the people Paul went out to in other countries listened. Back in Brooklyn the people at the bus stop mocked the brothers and repeated what they said, because they were entitled and comfortable.

Some are comfortable in the Israelite groups too: making money and merchandise off the people, fancy cars and houses, multiple wives who are all on EBT, but you’re a king. Diabolical. They are home. Our elders are second to Christ. Then why leave? Just stay. You’re already home.

“But the Jews stirred up the devout and honourable women, and the chief men of the city, and raised persecution against Paul and Barnabas, and expelled them out of their coasts.” The persecution was raised by betraying Jews. Paul and Barnabas got kicked out, exiled, deported out of the land because of their own people.

“Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? shall tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword?” No one. “As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long”: that is to be expected. “We are accounted as sheep for the slaughter. Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us.”

In this truth you have to prepare your mind and your body for persecution and tribulation. Many Israelites don’t want that, so they try to make captivity home: America’s not Babylon, the white man’s not Esau, so we’re home forever. If Esau isn’t the white man, then we are here till the end, and America stands forever. That is how those who play it safe try to avoid tribulation and persecution.

“Therefore I take pleasure in infirmities, in reproaches, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses for Christ’s sake: for when I am weak, then am I strong.” Paul makes it clear: he takes pleasure in persecutions, reproaches and distresses, because he knows it is for the Lord’s sake.

Persecution comes with this work. You can’t avoid it. That is why many Israelites choose not to join any group: they stay to themselves so they can blend in and hide among the world.

“So that we ourselves glory in you in the churches of God for your patience and faith in all your persecutions and tribulations that ye endure”: like Christ said in Matthew 24, endure unto the end. In this truth you have to endure persecutions and tribulations.

In Kenya the brothers were stoned, and Israelites laughed. The disciples got stoned, Paul got stoned. Here they tried a drive-by on the brothers, and tried to run them over. Many Israelites don’t want that. They teach where it’s safe: a white area downtown, cursing out white people all day, not the ghetto. They won’t go out of the country to find their people: all Israel is in America, or in Europe where the white man is, not in Africa. Have you been there? No. That is fear. You can afford multiple women but not a $100 passport. Diabolical.

“Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution.” The prophets suffered persecution; the apostles and the disciples, the same thing. Many Israelites don’t want that. They believe they are going to stand on the corner all day, curse out the white man and go home.

Some deny persecution entirely: locked up for five minutes, or can’t pay the light bill, and they call it persecution and tribulation. No, brother, that is falling on hard times. It is not persecution.

sense.text: Isaiah is prophesying against the elders and rulers of his time. “But they also have erred through wine, and through strong drink are out of the way”: out of the way of the Lord. “The priest and the prophet have erred through strong drink, they are swallowed up of wine.” People think these men are getting drunk. No: the wine and strong drink are doctrines, lies and falsehoods. “They err in vision, they stumble in judgment”: they don’t teach correctly. That is their erroneous doctrine.

“Whom shall he teach knowledge? and whom shall he make to understand doctrine?” If the priests and prophets are wicked as hell, who will God deal with? “Them that are weaned from the milk, and drawn from the breasts.” The milk is the word of God, and the breasts it comes from are the Old and New Testament, the Bible.

“For precept must be upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, and there a little.” Some Israelites say that isn’t what it means. That is exactly what it means. Each prophet the Most High dealt with was given a piece of the puzzle, and you put it together. Paul did it all the time, pulling from Psalms, from Isaiah, from Hosea, and putting it together. They didn’t have the Bible compiled back then. They had hundreds of scrolls: a scroll of David, a scroll of Proverbs, a scroll of Isaiah and one of Jeremiah, and they would read here and say, this goes with what Isaiah said right here. Paul was well learned and well studied, and he had it in his head.

It says precept upon precept, not precept upon commentary, not precept upon Blue Letter. Many Israelites are starting to listen to commentary and adopt apologetic methods: exegesis, eisegesis, hermeneutics, eight and nine different Bibles. That is confusion. It is adopting the doctrine of the oppressor. An apologist will say the word world is not in the Hebrew, it says ages. Then was it ages when Christ spoke to the world, or when the Pharisees said the world is going after him? Those are precepts, and they can’t argue with them. The precepts are what you use to destroy all the lies and doctrines.

A Bible that helps you understand the King James is fine; one that goes against it, no, because the King James Version and the precepts go hand in hand. Back in Bishop’s time, and before him, they were shutting down Times Square with precepts alone. Today some are getting fearful that the white man will confound them with the Greek, and they run to the Hebrew. The Most High still teaches knowledge and understanding of doctrine to those who keep the commandments and go precept upon precept, line upon line, here a little, there a little. That should be your method of teaching.

“For with stammering lips and another tongue will he speak to this people.” The Lord will bring us his word in different languages. It was fulfilled in the book of Acts, when the Lord put the spirit upon the disciples to speak his word in different languages, and it is fulfilled in our time. The disciples never told a man from Iraq or from Greece he had to learn Hebrew; the word was spoken to those who came to keep the feast days in their own language.

If the language were truly a necessity, why didn’t the Lord put the spirit on the foreign Jews who came to keep the Pentecost, so that they spoke the original tongue? Imagine speaking Russian all your life and speaking Hebrew in Jerusalem: that would be a miracle. It was not God’s plan. You are going to learn his word in all the places you are scattered, in Creole, Chichewa, Twi, French, Spanish, Swahili, Portuguese, Arabic, Amharic and Dutch. That is not denouncing the Hebrew, but Israel harps on it and gets confounded.

“This is the rest wherewith ye may cause the weary to rest; and this is the refreshing: yet they would not hear.” They would not listen. “But the word of the Lord was unto them precept upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, and there a little.”

Even in the law of Moses it is here a little, there a little. There is a prophecy of Christ in Numbers and a prophecy of Christ in Deuteronomy, and you put them together: the prophet we have to listen to in Deuteronomy 18 is the same as the angel in Exodus. Genesis 49 goes with Numbers 24. It is not just the prophets, it is Moses too, if you are keeping God’s commandments.

“That they might go, and fall backward, and be broken, and snared, and taken.” It was done that way on purpose, to cause the elders and rulers of our people to be confused, confounded and destroyed. That is why the Bible is not written plainly all the time, but in parables in some places: to confound the wicked of our people.

“Wherefore hear the word of the Lord, ye scornful men, that rule this people which is in Jerusalem. Because ye have said, We have made a covenant with death, and with hell are we at agreement”: the rulers of Israel today saying, we’re going to teach the nations can be saved, we’re going to teach Christianity, publicly or secretly, covertly or overtly.

“When the overflowing scourge shall pass through, it shall not come unto us”: we will not face persecution or any tribulation, we’ll be just fine, we’re going to play it safe. “For we have made lies our refuge”: that is the strong drink. “And under falsehood have we hid ourselves”: the white man is going to protect me. I teach you can be saved, I teach he’s not Esau, I’m safe.

precepts.why:
“If a man walking in the spirit and falsehood do lie, saying, I will prophesy unto thee of wine and of strong drink; he shall even be the prophet of this people.” That settles what the wine and strong drink of Isaiah 28 are: falsehood and lies.

It is not the priests and the prophets actually getting drunk and teaching. It is them pushing doctrines. The man walking in the spirit of falsehood prophesies wine and strong drink, and he becomes the prophet of this people.

sense.text:
“In those days went there out of Israel wicked men, who persuaded many, saying, Let us go and make a covenant with the heathen that are round about us”: with the so-called white man, the Greeks, the European man. That is the covenant with death and hell of Isaiah 28.

“For since we departed from them we have had much sorrow.” Since we took on these laws and commandments, we can’t follow them fully. We got to put that law stuff behind us. The law is done away with in Christ; we can do what we want in Christ; just believe in Christ and we’re good. Keeping them laws is like prison. They won’t say it to you outwardly, but that is the thinking in their mind.

“And made themselves uncircumcised.” How? “And forsook the holy covenant.” By forsaking the commandments of God they made themselves uncircumcised, heathen-minded. “And joined themselves to the heathen, and were sold to do mischief.”

precepts.why:
What “sold to do mischief” means is shown in the next chapter, in what the Greeks offered Mattathias. “Thou art a ruler, and an honourable and great man in this city”: a ruler in Modin, like the rulers in chapter 1 who said let’s go join the Greeks, but he didn’t give in. “And strengthened with sons and brethren”: a family to take care of. “Now therefore come thou first, and fulfil the king’s commandment, like as all the heathen have done, yea, and the men of Juda also, and such as remain at Jerusalem”: your own brothers joined us. “So shalt thou and thy house be in the number of the king’s friends, and thou and thy children shall be honoured with silver and gold, and many rewards.”

That is sold to do mischief: money. I’m going to teach Christianity because I want money. I’m going to teach against God’s laws because I want money. Nation salvation, because I want money, fame, fortune and the finer things in life. Mattathias said no, and because of it he faced persecution and tribulation: he and his sons became fugitives on the run, and many joined them and chose to be honourable and great as he was.

Many brothers today want honor and greatness in Babylon, not God’s greatness and honor. A captive does not get king privileges. Either you’re in captivity or you’re free. Whether you make four figures or seven, you are a slave here; in the eyes of the white man you are a rich slave. The gladiators of Rome had money, women and fame, and they were slaves. Football and basketball players, rappers and comedians are the same: told what to wear, what to say, what to spend. They made a covenant with death and hell, and when they speak up they lose everything, as happened to Ye, to Cannon and to Kyrie Irving. They are tools, set up as idols for us to worship and follow. They are sold to do mischief: selling their people out for fame and riches.

The covenant is a contract. They are under contract, which is why they get canceled when they say the wrong thing. Some may in time become a Nicodemus or a Joseph of Arimathea, who was rich and brave enough to go and get Christ’s body, risking his life. But regardless of tax bracket they are slaves like us: they’re in the house, we’re in the field. And that is why it is hard to cancel the Israelites: we never subscribed to their mischief and were never sold under their contract.

“Then gathered the chief priests and the Pharisees a council, and said, What do we? for this man doeth many miracles”: this man is doing amazing work. “If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.” The Romans, the white man, kept them in their seat of authority. Without the Romans they had no authority. So they had to get rid of Christ, who was taking away their following.

The Pharisees made a covenant with death and hell the same way our people did in the time of the Greeks and in Isaiah’s time. It is the same thing.

sense.text: “And have no root in themselves, and so endure but for a time”: the same as Matthew 13, a different type of Israelite. He has no root in himself: he doesn’t study and doesn’t apply. He endures for a time, but by and by he is offended, by persecution and tribulation: “afterward, when affliction or persecution ariseth for the word’s sake, immediately they are offended.”

“And these are they which are sown among thorns”: they are in the world, around the wicked. The thorns are the wicked. They dabble in the world: an Israelite on one hand and a gang affiliate on the other, pushing gang culture on one side and Israel on the other. You can’t serve both, or you’ll love one and hate the other.

“And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches”: sold to do mischief. “And the lusts of other things entering in”: a bunch of women, fame, fortune, to be well spoken of and glorified in this captivity. They “choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful”: right back in the world. They turn right back into a negro again.

“But there were false prophets also among the people, even as there shall be false teachers among you”: as Christ said, false prophets will arise in the time of tribulation, when iniquity abounds. In chapter 1 Peter speaks of his death; these arise after he is gone. As the truth spreads and persecution takes place, many of the prominent Israelite leaders, primarily of this camp, will be killed, locked up or exiled, and then the wicked Israelites, Christian and individualite alike, will come in to spread confusion.

That is what happened when Peter, Paul and John were dead. The church fathers came along, Justin Martyr, Tertullian, Augustine, Irenaeus, Ignatius, and pushed ideologies with the Bible. Most of them were into Greek philosophy and used the Greek way of thinking to interpret the Bible, and came out with the Trinity and the Logos, Greek metaphysics. Once John and Polycarp were dead and gone, madness arose. Justin Martyr taught the Trinity and that Christians could be good Romans and all be saved. He was a sellout, and he got martyred anyway. Many Israelites are doing the exact same thing: teach that everyone can be saved, avoid persecution, and live out captivity peacefully. That’s not how that works.

“Who privily shall bring in damnable heresies, even denying the Lord that bought them”: saying Christ had no color, that he was translucent and you couldn’t see him. “And bring upon themselves swift destruction.”

“And many shall follow their pernicious ways”: their lustful ways. “By reason of whom the way of truth shall be evil spoken of”: because of them. A man beats his wife, has multiple wives he doesn’t take care of, is abusive, sells drugs, is in a gang, and teaches the word of God, and the world says, that’s all in the camps, they’re a cult, a bunch of criminals. The word of God is spoken evil of because of you.

“And through covetousness”: money. “Shall they with feigned words”: lying words. “Make merchandise of you”: make money off of you, living off the people to buy fancy cars and get women and fame and the finer things in life. Teaching a doctrine for money and then going against it later. Teaching what you don’t really believe and making money off of it. “Whose judgment now of a long time lingereth not, and their damnation slumbereth not.”

“But chiefly them that walk after the flesh in the lust of uncleanness”: back to their pernicious ways. “And despise government”: they don’t like having leaders. They don’t want elders. I’m my own elder. They ask for counsel and don’t listen to it. They despise being told what to do. Israelites who stay to themselves despise government too, wanting to do their own thing and wander around; the Bible calls them wandering stars. “Presumptuous are they, selfwilled”: they do what they want.

“They are not afraid to speak evil of dignities.” Why does Peter say they are not afraid? It means you should be afraid. Bad things happen when you speak ill of the men before you. A man publicly cursed one of the men before us, and now all his own business is out there. Men call a Bishop a crooked cop and worse, with no evidence. Men say Malcolm X was a traitor who deserved to get killed, or that the men before us taught nation salvation, from a seventy-year-old book that turned up as a PDF out of nowhere. Badmouth the men before you and you’re going to find a seven- or eight-part video about you and what goes on in your house next. It never fails.

“Whereas angels, which are greater in power and might, bring not railing accusation against them before the Lord. But these, as natural brute beasts”: dummies, stupid animals, “made to be taken and destroyed”, made on purpose to be killed, “speak evil of the things that they understand not; and shall utterly perish in their own corruption”.

“And shall receive the reward of unrighteousness, as they that count it pleasure to riot in the day time”: doing what they want to do. “Having eyes full of adultery, and that cannot cease from sin”: having a bunch of women, because we know we ain’t in captivity. Can you afford them? No. King Solomon had his wives in their own place. Did Solomon have all 1,000 wives on EBT? What scripture is that? Maybe it’s in the Greek.

“Beguiling unstable souls”: making merchandise of suckers involved in the same evil they are involved in. “An heart they have exercised with covetous practices”: exercised with exquisite subtlety. Real good at it, real good at pushing that doctrine.

“Which have forsaken the right way, and are gone astray”, like Isaiah 28 says, out of the way, “following the way of Balaam the son of Bosor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness.” Balaam the witch loved money. The wages of unrighteousness: money, fame, fancy clothes, fancy cars, club hopping and bar hopping with other people’s money.

precepts.why:
Right at “an heart they have exercised with covetous practices”, go back to it: “There is an exquisite subtilty, and the same is unjust.” The one who is exquisitely subtle is wicked as hell, and you can’t see through the deception unless you keep God’s commandments. “And there is one that turneth aside to make judgment appear”: he makes it appear he is righteous, but he is wicked, deceiving himself.

The exquisite subtilty goes right back to the person who exercises himself with covetous practices: real manipulative, real slick, real cunning and conniving, but it is all about money. Read Peter again after it and it is the same man: “beguiling unstable souls: an heart they have exercised with covetous practices; cursed children”, “following the way of Balaam the son of Bosor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness”.

“Likewise also these filthy dreamers defile the flesh, despise dominion”: despise government, don’t like being told what to do. Orphans, no elders, kids governing kids. “And speak evil of dignities”: they don’t respect the elders.

Respecting your elders goes a long way. The understanding back then was not where it is now, but what they had, we used and built upon. The truth back then was small; now it has grown, and it is damn near a trend to be an Israelite. But it started with them, regardless of their mistakes or things they said. The Lord is our foundation first and foremost, but he used these men. If a man went off, did not Solomon go off? Should we throw away Ecclesiastes and Proverbs? David went off; throw Psalms in the garbage? Peter denied Christ. Moses made a mistake and didn’t get into the promised land; throw Moses away too? Israel is evil and dumb.

“Yet Michael the archangel, when contending with the devil he disputed about the body of Moses, durst not bring against him a railing accusation, but said, The Lord rebuke thee. But these speak evil of those things which they know not”, as Peter said, “but what they know naturally”: what they know emotionally, their feelings, “as brute beasts”, wild animals with no moral compass, “in those things they corrupt themselves.”

“Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain”: they hate their people, their brothers and their sisters. “And ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward”: they want money. “And perished in the gainsaying of Core”: they want position, rank and preeminence, like Core. Jude says the same as Peter: hatred, money and rank.

sense.text:
The Christian church is falling apart and people are leaving it in droves, while more and more are saying they are Israelites, especially seeing what the Israelis are doing on the news, bombing Gaza, Iran and Lebanon: these can’t be God’s people, so those guys must be right. So Christians are adapting. If you can’t beat them, join them: infiltrate, destroy, and take people back with you. A pastor on video says the Hebrew Israelites may be on to something about the slaves of the transatlantic slave trade, but that doesn’t mean he agrees with their theology: you can agree with the history but take up issues with the theology. Chosen people of God, we can roll with that; the laws, the feast days and the commandments, we ain’t doing that. They see the brothers marching in huge numbers and see money, not unity, order and structure: the wages of unrighteousness. Israelites going to Christianity to make money, and Christians going to the Israelites to make money. It is a crazy transitional time.

Then he says Deuteronomy is a book of law given to the Israelites of that time, not a book of prophecy. “I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren, like unto thee, and will put my words in his mouth; and he shall speak unto them all that I shall command him.” That is Christ. That is prophecy, in the law.

precepts.why:
“Behold, I send an Angel before thee, to keep thee in the way, and to bring thee into the place which I have prepared. Beware of him, and obey his voice, provoke him not; for he will not pardon your transgressions: for my name is in him.” This is the same prophet Deuteronomy 18 speaks of. He is called a Prophet in Deuteronomy and an Angel here in Exodus.

This is in the law. There are prophecies in the laws of Moses. These Christians are arrogantly ignorant.

“I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not nigh: there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel, and shall smite the corners of Moab, and destroy all the children of Sheth.” That is Christ there, and it is all Moses, all law.

“The sceptre shall not depart from Judah”: the same sceptre as Numbers 24. “Nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.” This prophecy is all in the five books of Moses.

That is why it is important for them to sit down with us rather than talk about us among themselves and make themselves look stupid.

sense.text:
They call this truth radical: anti-Semitic, anti-white, anti-LGBTQ, xenophobic and misogynistic. They separate it from the black Israelites who are converts, the friendly ones, the play-it-safe Israelites. Who are the radical ones? This room. The Bible is anti-LGBTQ, and it is not anti-Semitic at all, because it was written by Semites. These are all trigger words, and because of them laws are being passed to make it so this truth can’t be taught. It is going to be called anti-MAGA, anti-Trump.

“Therefore seeing we have this ministry, as we have received mercy, we faint not; but have renounced the hidden things of dishonesty, not walking in craftiness, nor handling the word of God deceitfully”: that is the exquisite subtlety. The Christian pastor saying we are the chosen people of God, while putting away God’s laws, is handling the word of God deceitfully. “But by manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man’s conscience in the sight of God.”

Paul gave the same warning Peter gave after his departure; Peter and Paul died around the same time. “For I know this, that after my departing”: after my death, as Peter said, “shall grievous wolves enter in among you, not sparing the flock”, to destroy the church. “Also of your own selves shall men arise”: among your own members, even amongst us right now, heretics rising up, “speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them”: pulling disciples out of the church after themselves.

“Therefore watch, and remember, that by the space of three years I ceased not to warn every one night and day with tears.” Be mindful. Paul saw it. It wasn’t if, it was when. When he was gone came all those evil church fathers, and the church split in half, east and west. It was chaos.
“Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved”: the sacrifice law. You must go back to the temple, be circumcised and keep the temple law in order to be saved.
“No small dissension and disputation”: it was a huge argument, a big debate, a big matter, so they went up to Jerusalem to the apostles and elders.

“There rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed”: followers, believers, quote unquote, “saying, That it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses”: after the manner of Moses, the sacrifice and the temple law. They were saying you had to return to sacrificing to be saved.

“And when there had been much disputing”: much arguing and debating. God gave the Gentiles the Holy Ghost as he did unto us, as with Cornelius, “and put no difference between us and them, purifying their hearts by faith.” The same people.

“That we trouble not them, which from among the Gentiles are turned to God”: they were from among the Gentiles, Israelites. Write unto them “that they abstain from pollutions of idols”, because idolatry was their main hang-up, “and from fornication”, sleeping around, “and from things strangled, and from blood. For Moses of old time hath in every city them that preach him, being read in the synagogues every sabbath day.” Their focus should be to abstain from idols, fornication and blood, and they could learn God’s laws from the synagogues.

“Then pleased it the apostles and elders, with the whole church, to send chosen men of their own company”, Judas surnamed Barsabas and Silas, “chief men among the brethren”: trusted men, chosen and acknowledged, sent with letters to certify that they were sent to teach this, because the Pharisees were infiltrating the church to push it back into Mosaic sacrificial law.

“Certain which went out from us have troubled you with words, subverting your souls, saying, Ye must be circumcised, and keep the law: to whom we gave no such commandment.” So they sent men they trusted, “Men that have hazarded their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ”, to tell them the same things by mouth and fix the confusion that had been spread.

“To lay upon you no greater burden than these necessary things; that ye abstain from meats offered to idols, and from blood, and from things strangled, and from fornication.” What this shows is the Pharisees trying to infiltrate the churches and causing trouble.

precepts.why:
“I marvel that ye are so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel”: another doctrine. “Which is not another”, because it is found in the law of Moses. “But there be some that trouble you”: the same men of Acts 15, which went out from among us, “and would pervert the gospel of Christ.”

“But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed.” Those men running around joining the churches and causing confusion by infiltration, let them be accursed. They were pushing a gospel we are no longer under: going back to sacrificing animals. That is another gospel.

Likewise today, Christians are going to come in here and do the same thing: push the same God’s people, but push Christianity. The same book, the same Bible, the same gospel, but something different. Accept the identity but not the theology. It is the same thing in reverse.

“And that because of false brethren unawares brought in, who came in privily to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus”: the liberty not to offer up animals anymore. Christ died on the cross, and we are free from that burden. “That they might bring us into bondage”: the bondage of sacrificing animals again to be saved, like Acts 15.

“Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage”: sacrifice. “If ye be circumcised, Christ shall profit you nothing”: being circumcised after the manner of Moses and sacrificing animals will not save you. “Ye are fallen from grace”: if animal sacrifice saves you, then Christ died for nothing. “But faith which worketh by love”: faith working by keeping God’s commandments, which must come first, before the circumcision.

“Ye did run well; who did hinder you”: you were doing a great job. “This persuasion cometh not of him that calleth you”: it doesn’t come from Christ. “A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump”: someone infiltrating the church. “But he that troubleth you shall bear his judgment”: the same men that troubled them in Acts 15 and in Thessalonians, accursed as Galatians 1 says. “I would they were even cut off which trouble you.”

“For, brethren, ye have been called unto liberty”: freed from offering animals. “Only use not liberty for an occasion to the flesh”: don’t use this freedom, this grace, to do what you want and sin, “but by love serve one another.”

“Seeing it is a righteous thing with God to recompense tribulation to them that trouble you”: these men were going through all the churches, Thessalonica, Galatia, causing confusion. “And to you who are troubled rest with us, when the Lord Jesus shall be revealed from heaven with his mighty angels”: those who are troubled, relax.

The troubling came from those Pharisees who believed, quote unquote, infiltrating the churches to bring them back to animal sacrifice and temple law, because that was their bread and butter.

“Little children, it is the last time: and as ye have heard that antichrist shall come, even now are there many antichrists.” “They went out from us”: Acts 15:24, they went out from us and troubled you. “But they were not of us”: that is the warning Paul gave, grievous wolves arising among you, not sparing the flock.

People leave out of here for no reason at all: I’m mad. Mad about what? I don’t know, I’m leaving. “For if they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us”: they would just stay. “But they went out, that they might be made manifest that they were not all of us.” They were not believers. They did not believe.

sense.text: The soldiers stripped Christ and put a scarlet robe and a crown of thorns on him, “and they bowed the knee before him, and mocked him, saying, Hail, King of the Jews! And they spit upon him, and took the reed, and smote him on the head.” They mocked Christ, spit on him and hit him on top of the head.

“And after that they had mocked him, they took the robe off from him, and put his own raiment on him, and led him away to crucify him.” We wear purple to commemorate Christ being mocked, because in the end he gets the glory. He gets the last laugh.

There are Israelites saying the movement isn’t taken seriously, that it’s a joke, because Drewski did a skit making fun of us. Christ was mocked; so we shouldn’t take him seriously either? Those are the talking points of a man who does not really believe at all and is slowly sliding into the world. Mike Epps mocked the Israelites back in 2013, and later apologized; before that they mocked the old school, 1 West. Mike Epps yesterday, Drewski today, Christ before that. It isn’t anything new.

When you are offended by and by, as Matthew 13 says, you leave and try to pull down what you learned with you, out of the embarrassment and shame of your sin being revealed and exposed: it’s not real, it’s not a community, it’s a joke. All you have to do is repent. Repentance is still open. Repent, instead of denying the Lord, because he says he will deny you in front of his Father.

precepts.why:
“Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, and all things that are written by the prophets concerning the Son of man shall be accomplished. For he shall be delivered unto the Gentiles”: the Romans, “and shall be mocked”. Christ said, I’m going to be made fun of; they’re going to mock me. “And spitefully entreated, and spitted on”: he was struck and spit on. What he told them happened.

“And they shall scourge him, and put him to death: and the third day he shall rise again.” They beat him and killed him, and he rose from the dead.

“And the Lord God of their fathers sent to them by his messengers, rising up betimes, and sending; because he had compassion on his people, and on his dwelling place: but they mocked the messengers of God, and despised his words, and misused his prophets”, killed them, “until the wrath of the Lord arose against his people, till there was no remedy.”

Christ was mocked, and before him the prophets were mocked. It is nothing new. To minimize the movement because it is mocked is a self-inflicted wound. It doesn’t make sense. It means you never really believed at all.

“Blessed are ye, when men shall hate you”: Christ said blessed are you when you’re hated, not loved, liked and accepted by everybody. “And when they shall separate you from their company”: not wanting to be around you. “And shall reproach you”: speaking evil of you. “And cast out your name as evil”: you’re part of a cult, you’re a psycho, a hate monger, you’re racist. “For the Son of man’s sake. Rejoice ye in that day, and leap for joy: for, behold, your reward is great in heaven: for in the like manner did their fathers unto the prophets.” They mocked the prophets, separated themselves from them and spoke evil of them. What happens to us today happened to our prophets yesterday.

“But woe unto you that are rich!”: they are about money, the wages of unrighteousness, “for ye have received your consolation.” “Woe unto you that are full!”: well off, money, fancy cars, “for ye shall hunger. Woe unto you that laugh now!”: that mock and make fun of us now, “for ye shall mourn and weep.” Laugh now, die later.

In this truth you are supposed to accept and face opposition and mockery, misuse, renouncing and denouncing. That is what the Bible says. The one who says otherwise is speaking from bitterness.

sense.text: “How that they told you there should be mockers in the last time”: the apostles saw it. Mockers in the last time, mocking the teachers of the gospel, “who should walk after their own ungodly lusts”: doing what they want to do.

“These be they who separate themselves, sensual, having not the Spirit.” These are the individualites, the wandering stars: I don’t need to be part of no camp, I’ll do my own thing. One of them puts out a list of the most dangerous Hebrew Israelite camps, and this camp is on it, for strict doctrine, discipline, a large following and global outreach, for teaching that Christ had a physical father, and for not dealing with water immersion. When did those become dangerous? When you’re black.

The individualites all speak bad about camps, but they learn from the camps. One sells shirts with fringes on the bottom; wearing fringes on the borders of your actual clothes started with this camp, when before that they were worn only on garments. You badmouth camps as dangerous, but sit down, learn from them, and sell shirts with what they teach to wear. If you sit there watching, engaged, taking notes, you are joining them, even if not physically. I don’t join no camps, just the scripture: that don’t make no damn sense.

Why do they want camps gone? Since the camps have been around, the truth has grown so much that when they are in the world doing worldly things, people ask: why you buying weed from me, why you in the club, why you smoking a Black & Mild, why you sleeping with them hoes, aren’t you an Israelite? They can’t hide no more. So they want camps gone, so they can blend back into the world and keep doing worldly, evil things.

precepts.why:
“Let us hold fast the profession of our faith without wavering; (for he is faithful that promised;) and let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works: not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is”: having not the spirit, sensual, devilish, emotional.

“But exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.” As you see the day of the end approaching, it is important to gather together.

“And have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness”: that is what individualites do. They have fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, out there in the world doing worldly things. When in Rome, do as the Romans do. “But rather reprove them”: they can’t, because they are doing the same thing.

“For it is a shame even to speak of those things which are done of them in secret. But all things that are reproved are made manifest by the light”: all things corrected are made manifest by God’s laws, “for whatsoever doth make manifest is light.”

Where did Paul get not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together? “Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired.” It is saying the same thing.

You cannot keep God’s laws unless you are part of a holy convocation. To convoke means to come together; that is what convocation means. Being on your own with your wife and kids is not a convocation; that’s a get-together. If we’re so evil, start your own: be the elder and have a convocation. Either way, you have to have a convocation or be part of one.

“And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light”: the world rather than God’s laws, his commandments, or Christ, “because their deeds were evil. For every one that doeth evil hateth the light”: they go away from the groups that keep God’s commandments, or with itching ears go toward groups that entertain their lust. I can have multiple hoes, I can get high and smoke weed, I don’t got to wear fringes, they can be saved: I’m going over there.

“Neither cometh to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved”: lest his actions be corrected. They don’t want correction. They despise dominion, despise government. “But he that doeth truth cometh to the light, that his deeds may be made manifest, that they are wrought in God.” You can’t do this alone. This truth is not made to be done alone. It is made to be done together as a family, a nation, not an individual.

sense.text:
These are the thoughts of the wicked. “Doctrine unto fools is as fetters on the feet”: the doctrine, the laws of God, to a fool is like being handcuffed or being in prison. They can’t stand it. “And like manacles on the right hand”: handcuffs on the hands.

I can’t do nothing, man. I ain’t joining that group. I agree with the history but not the theology. Because the laws, doctrines and commandments of God are fetters on their feet and manacles on their hands, they have no freedom in their mind when keeping God’s laws. It is prison to them. So they stay to themselves and stay separate.

“I know thy works, that thou art neither cold nor hot”: you are playing around, in between, jumping the fence. “I would thou wert cold or hot”: make a choice between being cold in the world, waxing cold in evil, or waxing hot and fervent in the truth.

“So then because thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot”: because you are in the middle, playing games, with one foot in the world and one toe in the Bible. “I will spue thee out of my mouth”: I’m going to destroy you.

“Because thou sayest, I am rich”: you are content, “and increased with goods, and have need of nothing”: I stand by myself, I don’t need to join nobody. “And knowest not that thou art wretched, and miserable, and poor, and blind, and naked”: sinful, and you don’t acknowledge that you are sinful.

“Now it is high time to awake out of sleep: for now is our salvation nearer than when we believed.” That is where we are right now. “The night is far spent”: time is almost up here. “The day is at hand”: the day of the Lord is at hand. “Let us therefore cast off the works of darkness”: let’s stop doing worldly things, come out of the world and come into this truth, “and let us put on the armour of light.”

“Let us walk honestly, as in the day”: not handling the word of God deceitfully. “Not in rioting and drunkenness”: rioting, sleeping around, messing around with hoes. “Not in chambering and wantonness”: lust. “Not in strife and envying”: hatred. “But put ye on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make not provision for the flesh, to fulfil the lusts thereof.”

“For I think that God hath set forth us the apostles last, as it were appointed to death”: to be killed, to die. “For we are made a spectacle unto the world, and to angels, and to men.” That is what people don’t want. They want to be Israelites but hide somewhere under a tree. If you are going to be in this truth, you have to be a light that shines on a mountaintop. You can’t be an Israelite and hide and blend in.

That is why they want camps gone: camps put this truth in the forefront. They don’t want to be in the forefront; they want to hide in the background. You’re going to die in the background too.

“We are fools for Christ’s sake, but ye are wise in Christ; we are weak, but ye are strong; ye are honourable, but we are despised”: not loved, mocked. “Even unto this present hour we both hunger, and thirst, and are naked, and are buffeted, and have no certain dwellingplace; and labour, working with our own hands: being reviled”: slandered, lied on, “we bless; being persecuted, we suffer it: being defamed”: spoken ill of. We’re xenophobic, anti-LGBTQ, anti-white, anti-Semitic: we are defamed.

“We are made as the filth of the world, and are the offscouring of all things unto this day.” Rejected, but the Lord doesn’t reject us. The Lord has our back.

precepts.why: “Partly, whilst ye were made a gazingstock both by reproaches and afflictions”: all of us in this truth are made to be seen, made a gazingstock, the same spectacle unto the world the apostles were. Reproaches are hatred, and afflictions. “And partly, whilst ye became companions of them that were so used.”

sense.text:
“Whosoever therefore shall be ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation”: ashamed of the Lord, ashamed of doing the Lord’s work. That is the one trying to find a lukewarm common ground: a Christian on this side and an Israelite on that side, or staying to himself and being part of nobody. That is playing games, trying to be lukewarm.

“Of him also shall the Son of man be ashamed, when he cometh in the glory of his Father with the holy angels.”
